paragraphs.text: And I, brethren, could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, as unto babes in Christ.
paragraphs.original: Κἀγώ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλʼ ὡς σαρκίνοις, ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ.
paragraphs.translit: Kagō, adelphoi, ouk ēdynēthēn lalēsai hymin hōs pneumatikois allʼ hōs sarkinois, hōs nēpiois en Christō.

paragraphs.text: I fed you with milk, not with meat; for ye were not yet able [to bear it]: nay, not even now are ye able;
paragraphs.original: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα, οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε. ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε,
paragraphs.translit: gala hymas epotisa, ou brōma, oupō gar edynasthe. allʼ oude eti nyn dynasthe,

paragraphs.text: for ye are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you jealousy and strife, are ye not carnal, and do ye not walk after the manner of men?
paragraphs.original: ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;
paragraphs.translit: eti gar sarkikoi este. hopou gar en hymin zēlos kai eris, ouchi sarkikoi este kai kata anthrōpon peripateite;

paragraphs.text: For when one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are ye not men?
paragraphs.original: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις· Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἕτερος δέ· Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ, οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε;
paragraphs.translit: hotan gar legē tis· Egō men eimi Paulou, heteros de· Egō Apollō, ouk anthrōpoi este;

paragraphs.text: What then is Apollos? and what is Paul? Ministers through whom ye believed; and each as the Lord gave to him.
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς; τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος; διάκονοι διʼ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε, καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ κύριος ἔδωκεν.
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun estin Apollōs; ti de estin Paulos; diakonoi diʼ hōn episteusate, kai hekastō hōs ho kyrios edōken.

paragraphs.text: I planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα, Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν, ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς ηὔξανεν·
paragraphs.translit: egō ephyteusa, Apollōs epotisen, alla ho theos ēuxanen·

paragraphs.text: So then neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων, ἀλλʼ ὁ αὐξάνων θεός.
paragraphs.translit: hōste oute ho phyteuōn estin ti oute ho potizōn, allʼ ho auxanōn theos.

paragraphs.text: Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: but each shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
paragraphs.original: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν, ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον,
paragraphs.translit: ho phyteuōn de kai ho potizōn hen eisin, hekastos de ton idion misthon lēmpsetai kata ton idion kopon,

paragraphs.text: For we are God`s fellow-workers: ye are God`s husbandry, God`s building.
paragraphs.original: θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί· θεοῦ γεώργιον, θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
paragraphs.translit: theou gar esmen synergoi· theou geōrgion, theou oikodomē este.

paragraphs.text: According to the grace of God which was given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder I laid a foundation; and another buildeth thereon. But let each man take heed how he buildeth thereon.
paragraphs.original: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα, ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ. ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ·
paragraphs.translit: Kata tēn charin tou theou tēn dotheisan moi hōs sophos architektōn themelion ethēka, allos de epoikodomei. hekastos de blepetō pōs epoikodomei·

paragraphs.text: For other foundation can no man lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός·
paragraphs.translit: themelion gar allon oudeis dynatai theinai para ton keimenon, hos estin Iēsous Christos·

paragraphs.text: But if any man buildeth on the foundation gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, stubble;
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν, ἄργυρον, λίθους τιμίους, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην,
paragraphs.translit: ei de tis epoikodomei epi ton themelion chryson, argyron, lithous timious, xyla, chorton, kalamēn,

paragraphs.text: each man`s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself shall prove each man`s work of what sort it is.
paragraphs.original: ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται, ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει· ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται, καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει.
paragraphs.translit: hekastou to ergon phaneron genēsetai, hē gar hēmera dēlōsei· hoti en pyri apokalyptetai, kai hekastou to ergon hopoion estin to pyr auto dokimasei.

paragraphs.text: If any man`s work shall abide which he built thereon, he shall receive a reward.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν, μισθὸν λήμψεται·
paragraphs.translit: ei tinos to ergon menei ho epoikodomēsen, misthon lēmpsetai·

paragraphs.text: If any man`s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as through fire.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται, ζημιωθήσεται, αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται, οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός.
paragraphs.translit: ei tinos to ergon katakaēsetai, zēmiōthēsetai, autos de sōthēsetai, houtōs de hōs dia pyros.

paragraphs.text: Know ye not that ye are a temple of God, and [that] the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?
paragraphs.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: Ouk oidate hoti naos theou este kai to pneuma tou theou oikei en hymin;

paragraphs.text: If any man destroyeth the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, and such are ye.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ θεός· ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν, οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: ei tis ton naon tou theou phtheirei, phtherei touton ho theos· ho gar naos tou theou hagios estin, hoitines este hymeis.

paragraphs.text: Let no man deceive himself. If any man thinketh that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool, that he may become wise.
paragraphs.original: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω· εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, μωρὸς γενέσθω, ἵνα γένηται σοφός,
paragraphs.translit: Mēdeis heauton exapatatō· ei tis dokei sophos einai en hymin en tō aiōni toutō, mōros genesthō, hina genētai sophos,

paragraphs.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, He that taketh the wise in their craftiness:
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν· γέγραπται γάρ· Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hē gar sophia tou kosmou toutou mōria para tō theō estin· gegraptai gar· Ho drassomenos tous sophous en tē panourgia autōn·

paragraphs.text: and again, The Lord knoweth the reasonings of the wise that they are vain.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάλιν· Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin· Kyrios ginōskei tous dialogismous tōn sophōn hoti eisin mataioi.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore let no one glory in men. For all things are yours;
paragraphs.original: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: hōste mēdeis kauchasthō en anthrōpois· panta gar hymōn estin,

paragraphs.text: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; all are yours;
paragraphs.original: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: eite Paulos eite Apollōs eite Kēphas eite kosmos eite zōē eite thanatos eite enestōta eite mellonta, panta hymōn,

paragraphs.text: and ye are Christ`s; and Christ is God`s.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de Christou, Christos de theou.
